intro: The first release in May 2026 had three workflows and human gates. 4.x grew to measure itself, and the measurements said most of the ceremony was pure cost. 5.0 keeps the parts that pay, with {commands} commands.

entries.title: Initial release
entries.body: `/plan`, `/code` and `/review`, plus `/ship` end to end. Every stage stops for your approval. The first guardrail hooks and the global ruleset (SOLID, clean code, OWASP).

entries.title: Audit-driven overhaul
entries.body: Hooks now load on a clean marketplace install. Their output schema was fixed; reminders and lint feedback had been silently dropped.

entries.title: Discovery
entries.body: `/discover` turns a product idea into a researched, traceable requirements set (BRD, SRS, FRD, SDD, TDD) that planning consumes.

entries.title: Critical thinking and parallel review
entries.body: Agents challenge the premise of a request. `/review-panel` runs several review lenses at once. `/code-parallel` builds independent iterations in isolated worktrees.

entries.title: The execution brief
entries.body: An expensive model front-loads research and decisions into a dense `brief.md`. A cheaper model executes against it without researching again. 1.1.1 moved CI and publishing onto hashira.

entries.title: Trust core and deterministic loops
entries.body: Loop caps and the findings ledger move from model discipline into tested scripts, with durable state a loop can resume from. New lifecycle commands: `/debug`, `/pr`, `/adopt`, `/atlas`, `/impact`, `/upgrade`, `/release-readiness`, `/incident`.

entries.title: Portable runtime
entries.body: The whole runtime was ported from bash and jq to zero-dependency Node and runs natively on Windows. Each port was checked byte for byte against 152 golden fixtures.

entries.title: Reasoning craft and a front door
entries.body: Writing guidance became detectors every agent runs (drift, hedge, horoscope, deletion). The `somi` front-door agent routes a plain request to the right flow on Copilot.

entries.title: Cost tiers
entries.body: Each agent gets a `low`, `medium` or `high` tier, resolved at dispatch. 3.1 made agents work on GitHub Copilot and stopped reporting a tier as applied when it wasn't.

entries.title: Hard cost cap, native agents, sized delivery, measurement

highlights.title: Control
items: **The cost ceiling is a hard cap**, with an override for each agent. Lowering a tier needs your confirmation.
**Native `somi-*` agents.** An agent starts as the type the host registered, or not at all; there is no stand-in prompt.
**Model preference lists** for each host, a model picker in `/somi-config`, and a warning when a host has no mapping.
**One global config** every project reads, with each repo's `.somi/config.json` merged over it; config reads follow junctions and symlinks (4.0.1).

highlights.title: Delivery
items: **`/ship-loop` sizes the work first:** trivial, small or full. Small work skips the planning ceremony.
**A security lens from the sizing record:** work that handles untrusted input is always reviewed by the security reviewer.
**Repair passes re-review only what changed since the last review**, an optional wall-time budget, and a record of how each agent was dispatched.

entries.title: A front door that only dispatches
entries.body: The `somi` agent no longer runs procedures itself: it picks one workflow and hands it to the `somi-flow` runner, or to `somi-general` when nothing fits, and relays the runner's questions to you as checkpoints. Every workflow's procedure is now one flow skill shared by its command and the runner, and the largest agents load their procedures from role skills. 4.1.1 lets the loops read plan files saved with CRLF on Windows and take review findings from a file.

entries.title: Your agent in charge, SoMi advising

highlights.title: Routing that costs less
items: **Your agent holds the conversation** on medium, as a bare agent would, and asks `somi_route` for the workflow when a ticket, large work or an unclear request needs one. SoMi keeps no workflow state, so nothing refuses your next request.
**Six commands, everything else in the chat:** `/somi`, `/somi-deliver` for large work in stages, `/somi-review`, `/somi-quality`, `/somi-status` and `/somi-config`.
**Shards** connect another plugin's skill, agent or tool to a named step.

highlights.title: Better code, measured
items: **A quality gate** scores what a change adds for complexity, nesting, length, parameters, copies and suppressions. When a turn that changed code ends, anything over a limit goes back to be fixed, on Claude Code and Copilot CLI.
**One reviewer per change,** decided from the real diff: the security reviewer alone on a boundary.
**On the registered benchmark,** 90 of 96 draws solved against bare's 72, at 1.28x bare's cost per solved task.
**5.0.1** gives the quality gate a time limit you can set, so a large change is checked instead of cut off.
**5.0.2** skips the gate on a turn that changed nothing, and reads files in batches, about three times faster on a large branch.

open: Routing has not yet been measured on work large enough to need it: on single-change tasks the agent rarely routes, and the router misses most bug reports written in new words. That comes next.
